title: Non-financial factors in credit

draft.title: Non-financial factors in credit
card: Credit decisions use numbers, such as the amount owed and the days to pay. They also use non-financial factors, which are things that cannot be measured in dollars straight away.
Customer goodwill
the good feeling and loyalty of customers. A business may allow a loyal customer extra time to pay, because it hopes to keep their future sales.
Supplier reliability
how well a supplier delivers the right goods on time and in good condition. A business may keep buying on credit from a reliable supplier, even if another supplier offers a slightly lower price.
Reputation
what others think of the business. Paying on time and treating customers fairly builds a good reputation, which makes suppliers more willing to offer credit.
draft.remember: Credit choices weigh trust, reliability and reputation as well as the numbers.

a.q: Which of these is a non-financial factor in a business's decision to sell on credit?
opts: A long-standing customer who has always been loyal
The total amount a customer owes at the end of June
The number of days a customer takes to pay
The value of sales made on credit last month
a.why: A customer's loyalty is goodwill, which cannot be measured in dollars straight away. The other three are amounts or days, which are numbers taken from the records.
a.clue: Which one cannot be read off the accounting records as a figure?

b.q: Ravi's hardware store in Geelong can buy timber on credit from two suppliers. Supplier X is 3% cheaper but often delivers late. Supplier Y delivers on time every time. Which reason best supports choosing Y?
opts: Its reliability keeps Ravi's shelves stocked for customers
Its price is lower, so Ravi will pay less on each order
Its goods are sure to have a longer credit period
Its supplier is certain to offer Ravi a discount later
b.why: Reliable delivery is a non-financial factor. It helps Ravi keep customers and his reputation, even though X costs less. The other options are about price, credit period or discounts, and the story does not say any of them is true for Y.
b.clue: Look for the reason that is not about price or amounts.

a.best: A long-standing customer who has always been loyal

b.best: Its reliability keeps Ravi's shelves stocked for customers

problems.detail: The right option stands out. Two distractors carry absolute words ('sure to', 'certain to'), and the right option is the only one using the card's own term 'reliability'. A student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The option 'Its supplier is certain to offer Ravi a discount later' is ungrammatical. Y is itself the supplier, so 'Its supplier' makes no sense.

The clue 'Look for the reason that is not about price or amounts' rules out the three distractors, which mention price, credit period and discount. That leaves only the answer, so the clue gives it away.

check.summary: The card and question a are sound. In question b the right answer is too easy to spot: the distractors use 'sure' and 'certain', the right option repeats the card's word 'reliability', and the clue removes the other options. One distractor also says 'Its supplier' when Y is the supplier.
